inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to keep retrying or spawning researchers until every row is complete, with no termination bound.
The design relies on prompt behavior without structural limits on retries, runtime, spawning, or spend.

elements.name: Nightly CRM row batch into agent
Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Prompt directs completion of every row
controls.decay_rationale: This is not a real limiting control; the prompt encourages persistence and retries rather than bounding them, so it cannot reliably prevent runaway tool use.

controls.name: Missing hard limits on steps runtime retries and sub agents
Missing spend cap and alert on enrichment account
Missing cap on recursive sub agent spawning

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries and recursive delegation can exhaust shared paid API quota
findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor reaches high because the only declared control is a behavioral prompt rule, but that text is itself the mechanism driving the runaway condition: it instructs the agent to retry or spawn researchers and to keep going until every row is complete, while the runtime notes say malformed rows never return a complete result and there are no hard limits on steps, retries, runtime, or sub agents. That design fact makes the credited behavioral control non-mitigating in practice, so residual remains critical.

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps or runtime per nightly batch rises, or sub agent count per row increases.

evidence.observation: The prompt says to retry or spawn a researcher when lookup is incomplete and to keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call and uses a shared monthly quota; when the quota runs out, other business tools stop working until the next month.
The nightly batch is 40000 rows and about 3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Enforce hard limits on retries, total tool calls, runtime, and recursion depth per row and per batch.
Apply a hard spend cap and quota alert that preserves reserved capacity for sales and marketing workloads.
Revise the prompt so malformed or repeatedly failing rows are skipped to exception handling instead of retried until complete.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe one first party batch agent and no inbound identity or peer authentication surface to assess for spoofing.
The artifacts do not show self modification, tool definition updates, or writable prompt or config paths that would create a present tampering issue.
This case centers on quota exhaustion, and the artifacts do not describe disputed action attribution or audit records needed for a repudiation assessment.
The described design uses paid lookups and CRM writes, but the artifacts do not evidence a present confidential data disclosure path.
No evidence shows the agent obtaining broader authority than intended; the shared key raises blast radius for availability, not privilege escalation.
The nightly CRM batch is modeled as an internal source and the artifacts do not describe impersonation or identity verification weaknesses on that source.
No dispute about authorship or transaction attribution is evidenced for the CRM source in the provided artifacts.
The issue is depletion of a shared quota by legitimate but uncontrolled use, not unauthorized modification of the quota store itself.
The quota and key store are described only in terms of shared consumption and outage impact, not data exposure.
The present issue is absence of limits in configuration, not evidence of unauthorized modification of configuration by an attacker or the agent.
The artifacts do not describe secrets or sensitive records exposed from configuration storage.
The artifacts do not say whether the outbound API path has integrity protection, request signing, or transport controls.
The artifacts do not specify encryption, payload logging, or whether account row fields sent to the provider include sensitive content.

rating.rationale: Present design has a high consequence denial of service property finding: an A4 autonomous batch agent with recursive delegation, no hard limits on retries, steps, runtime, or spawning, and no spend alert can exhaust a shared paid API quota. No declared structural preventive or containment control narrows the sink today; the only declared prompt behavior is dependent and does not limit the path. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No runtime configuration, orchestration policy, billing guardrail configuration, or telemetry was provided, so absence of hard spend and execution limits is assessed from the notes as declared design.
No MCP, API auth, or transport security artifacts were provided, so protocol integrity and confidentiality checks could only be marked not assessed where relevant.
